1"""Registration table for the unary ``aten::_foreach_*`` family. 

2 

3Thirty operators share one multi-tensor executor. They differ only in the 

4element-wise math, the output dtype policy, and which dtypes ATen accepts, so 

5each one is a table row rather than a copy of the wrapper. The element-wise 

6math is *reused* from the existing single-tensor FlagGems implementations by 

7taking the ``triton.jit`` scalar function out of their ``pointwise_dynamic`` 

8wrapper -- no formula is written twice. 

9 

10The dtype policies below were measured against the pinned PyTorch build (see 

11``kernelgen_work/EVIDENCE/foreach_family/unary_probe.log``); they are not 

12inferred from operator names. Notable measured facts: 

13 

14* Transcendentals promote every integral and bool input to ``float32``, while 

15 ``ceil``/``floor``/``round``/``trunc``/``frac``/``neg``/``sign`` preserve the 

16 input dtype. 

17* The exclusions differ per operator: ``floor`` rejects ``bool`` but accepts 

18 all integers, ``frac`` rejects all integers, ``sign`` accepts ``bool`` but 

19 rejects complex, ``erf``/``erfc``/``lgamma`` reject complex. 

20* Only ``abs`` maps complex to real; it is the one operator whose output dtype 

21 differs from its input for a complex input. 

22"""

91def _scalar_fn(pointwise_fn) -> Callable: 

92 """The bare ``triton.jit`` function inside a ``pointwise_dynamic`` wrapper. 

93 

94 ``pointwise_dynamic`` keeps the user's scalar function so it can splice the 

95 source into a generated module; the foreach executor needs exactly the same 

96 object as a ``tl.constexpr`` callable. Reaching for it is what lets thirty 

97 operators reuse the repository's existing math instead of restating it. 

98 """ 

99 return pointwise_fn._scalar_fn 

100 

101 

102# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

103# 16-bit approximation path 

104# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

105# 

106# ``erf``/``erfc``/``lgamma`` spend 20-25 fp32 instructions per element in 

107# libdevice's range reduction and polynomial. A 16-bit result does not need 

108# that: fp16 has ~5e-4 relative resolution and the suite tolerance is 

109# rtol=1e-3/atol=1e-4 (bf16 rtol=1.6e-2). The fitted minimax bodies below 

110# measured, in-place at 512^2 x 16 fp16, erfc 19.97 -> 11.55 us, erf 15.65 -> 

111# 11.87 us and lgamma 31.90 -> 27.81 us. The coefficients are final 

112# exact-minimax (LP) fits -- do not refit them. 

113# 

114# ``atan`` has both bodies. ``_atan_func`` is accurate to 2 ulp in fp32 and is 

115# what out-of-place, fp32 in-place and the complex path run; ``_atan16_func`` is 

116# the same reduction with a degree-3 polynomial, which is all a 16-bit *store* 

117# can resolve (1 fp16/bf16 ulp worst case over 200k points) and measured 

118# 32.50 -> 29.38 us (fp16) and 31.55 -> 30.27 us (bf16) against the body it 

119# replaces at 1024^2 x 16. Being cheaper is not the only reason it is there: 

120# the old ``c = (a-1)/(a+1) = 1 - 2/(a+1)`` form cancels when ``a`` is small, so 

121# the result there was noise -- ``x = -2.5e-8`` came out as ``0.0`` -- and that 

122# body had to go regardless of its speed. 

123# 

124# ``acos`` and ``asin`` were fitted too and rejected: both are already at the 

125# memory floor (measured -0.64 us and -0.13 us against libdevice), so their 

126# rows keep the accurate function. 

127# 

128# Sign is applied with ``_sgn_where``, not ``copysign``: the libdevice call 

129# measured ~0.7 us per call on this device and the two element selects are 

130# worth 1.2-1.8 us in total. 

131# 

132# ``lgamma`` needs the *accurate* ``sin`` in the reflection, not 

133# ``fast_sinf``. The fast variant measured -9.92 us (21.63 against 27.81 us) 

134# but is unusable: its absolute error floor is ~2^-22, and the argument is 

135# reduced to [-pi/2, pi/2] where ``sin`` crosses zero, so ``log|sin|`` turns 

136# that floor into an error large enough to push 6089 fp16 inputs outside 

137# rtol=1e-3. The accurate ``sin`` costs the recurrence far less than the 

138# reflection's logarithm saves. 

139# 

140# ``fn16`` is consumed by the in-place entry point only. An in-place call 

141# costs ~27 us of host CPU, under ``do_bench``'s L2-flush window, so host work 

142# is free and the kernel time is what is measured. An out-of-place call costs 

143# ~57 us, past the window, so any added Python leaks 1:1 into the measured 

144# latency while the kernel time the fast body saves stays hidden underneath 

145# it; the same gate enabled there measured +0.3 to +1.3 us on these rows (the 

146# fast-math lane measured 1.3-3.7 us on its own). The accurate body is free on 

147# that path, so out-of-place deliberately keeps ``op.fn``. Do not "restore the 

148# symmetry" -- see ``apply_unary``. 

149# 

150# The executor hands these functions a value already cast to the output dtype, 

151# so every body widens to fp32 first; the result is cast back on store. 

152 

153 

154@triton.jit 

155def _sgn_where(v, x): 

156 """``v`` with the sign of ``x``, preserving ``+-0`` (no ``copysign``).""" 

157 return tl.where(x > 0.0, v, tl.where(x < 0.0, -v, x)) 

158 

159 

160@triton.jit 

161def _erfc_pos_func(x): 

162 """``erfc(|x|)``: ``exp(a*(Q(a) - a))`` with ``v = a/3 - 1``. 

163 

164 The leading factor of ``a`` makes the polynomial argument exactly 0 at 

165 ``a = 0``, so ``erfc(0) = 1`` and ``erf(+-0) = +-0`` come out exact; the 

166 negative leading coefficient gives ``exp(-inf) = 0`` for ``a = inf``. 

167 """ 

168 a = tl.abs(x) 

169 v = a * 0.33333334 - 1.0 

170 q = ( 

171 ( 

172 (((-0.0073543065 * v + 0.02308265) * v - 0.0400557) * v + 0.072947204) * v 

173 - 0.14141525 

174 ) 

175 * v 

176 + 0.27006385 

177 ) * v - 0.5734953 

178 return tl_extra_shim.fast_expf(a * (q - a)) 

179 

180 

181@triton.jit 

182def _approx_erfc_func(x): 

183 """``erfc(x)`` for all x: ``erfc(-a) = 2 - erfc(a)``.""" 

184 x = x.to(tl.float32) 

185 e = _erfc_pos_func(x) 

186 return tl.where(x >= 0.0, e, 2.0 - e) 

187 

188 

189@triton.jit 

190def _approx_erf_func(x): 

191 """``erf(x) = sign(x)*(1 - erfc(|x|))``; exact ``+-0`` and ``+-1``. 

192 

193 Reusing the erfc body measured 15.65 -> 11.87 us in-place. The exp-free 

194 direct polynomial (14 coefficients) was fitted and rejected at 14.30 us. 

195 """ 

196 x = x.to(tl.float32) 

197 return _sgn_where(1.0 - _erfc_pos_func(x), x) 

198

200@triton.jit 

201def _atan_func(x): 

202 """``atan(x)`` through ``c = min(a, 1/a)``, ``a = |x|``, and one polynomial. 

203 

204 ``atan(c) = c*(pi/4 + (1 - c*c)*S(2c*c - 1))`` anchors both ends, so the 

205 degree-8 fit needs no correction term, ``1 - c*c`` is evaluated as 

206 ``0.5 - 0.5*v`` (which removes the second squaring), and the ``a > 1`` 

207 branch is one subtraction from ``pi/2``. It is the same split libdevice 

208 uses, minus its two IEEE-correctly-rounded reciprocals: ``fast_dividef`` is 

209 a single ``MUFU.RCP``, so no exponent guard, branch and slow-path call. 

210 

211 Accuracy, measured on 9.4M fp32 values against ``atan`` in double (max 

212 / mean ulp distance, share above 1 ulp): this body 2.0 / 0.30 / 0.02%, 

213 libdevice 1.0 / 0.13 / 0% but 0.1% of them (all subnormal inputs, where 

214 libdevice flushes to zero) are further off than 4 ulp, ATen 1.0 / 0.13 / 

215 0%. Against the libdevice output it replaces, this body agrees within 

216 half an ulp on 78% of values, within 1 ulp on 99.9% and within 2 ulp on 

217 all of them (subnormals excluded, where it is the *more* accurate of the 

218 two); on a 1024^2 x 16 ``randn`` list the same bound holds -- 33.6% of the 

219 16.7M fp32 entries differ, 2 ulp worst case. ATen's own ``atan`` is 

220 further from libdevice than that on 0.23% of values, at 2 ulp. ``+-0``, 

221 ``+-1``, ``+-inf``, ``+-pi/2`` and NaN are bit-identical to libdevice. 

222 Rounded to fp16, the two agree on all but 0.01% of that list (1 ulp) and 

223 in bf16 on every entry. 

224 

225 Cost: measured through the executor kernel at 1024^2 x 16, 46.7 -> 33.0 us 

226 (fp16), 47.3 -> 35.4 us (bf16) and 56.0 -> 41.5 us (fp32), i.e. level with 

227 ``torch.atan`` on one concatenated tensor (31.9 / 33.1 / 40.0 us), at 32 

228 registers and no spills against 38/48. It is also faster in every dtype at 

229 512^2 (16.7/16.5/18.8 -> 12.8/13.3/15.0 us) and 256^2 (9.2/9.6/10.3 -> 

230 7.6/7.9/8.4 us). The exact ``min``/``select`` shape was previously 

231 rejected here on a 512^2 in-place measurement (12.35 against 12.22 us); 

232 that gap does not reproduce at 1024^2, where the reduction is worth 1.7 us 

233 against the ``(a-1)/(a+1)`` form. The sign is two bit operations, not 

234 ``_sgn_where``: on the same polynomial the two element selects measured 

235 35.74 against 32.19 us. 

236 

237 This is the only body the out-of-place entry point runs, in every dtype; 

238 the in-place 16-bit path takes ``_atan16_func`` instead. 

239 """ 

240 x = x.to(tl.float32) 

241 a = tl.abs(x) 

242 c = tl.minimum(a, tl_extra_shim.fast_dividef(1.0, a)) 

243 v = 2.0 * c * c - 1.0 

244 s = ( 

245 ( 

246 ( 

247 ( 

248 ( 

249 ( 

250 (6.0314509938e-06 * v - 1.5670237190e-05) * v 

251 + 4.3488384108e-05 

252 ) 

253 * v 

254 - 1.5755316417e-04 

255 ) 

256 * v 

257 + 5.6417664746e-04 

258 ) 

259 * v 

260 - 2.0681463648e-03 

261 ) 

262 * v 

263 + 7.9936748371e-03 

264 ) 

265 * v 

266 - 3.3709898591e-02 

267 ) * v + 1.7004318535e-01 

268 core = c * (0.7853982 + (0.5 - 0.5 * v) * s) 

269 res = tl.where(a > 1.0, 1.5707964 - core, core) 

270 return ( 

271 res.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) | (x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) & -2147483648) 

272 ).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

273 

274 

275@triton.jit 

276def _atan16_func(x): 

277 """``atan(x)`` for a 16-bit *store*: ``_atan_func``'s reduction, degree 3. 

278 

279 Same ``c = min(a, 1/a)`` reduction, same anchored ``c*(pi/4 + (1-c*c)*S)`` 

280 shape and same sign handling; only the polynomial is shorter. Degree 3 is 

281 the stopping point, not a compromise: over 200k points in ``c`` in (0, 1] 

282 the minimax fit's relative error is 3.3e-05, i.e. 0.07 of an fp16 ulp and 

283 0.004 of a bf16 ulp, and more coefficients cannot improve a result that is 

284 then rounded to 11 (or 8) mantissa bits. Measured on the harness cells 

285 against ``atan`` in float64 rounded to the storage dtype: bf16 agrees 

286 bit-for-bit on every entry, fp16 within 1 ulp on every entry (2.8% of them 

287 1 ulp away) -- the same 1 ulp worst case as ATen's own ``atan``, which is 

288 0.01% away. ``+-0``, ``+-inf``, ``+-pi/2`` and NaN are exact. 

289 

290 The ``min`` reduction is what makes this usable near zero, where the body 

291 it replaces cancelled: ``atan(x) -> x`` as ``x -> 0``, and ``c = a`` there. 

292 """ 

293 x = x.to(tl.float32) 

294 a = tl.abs(x) 

295 c = tl.minimum(a, tl_extra_shim.fast_dividef(1.0, a)) 

296 v = 2.0 * c * c - 1.0 

297 s = ( 

298 (-2.8894221779e-03 * v + 8.2041949608e-03) * v - 3.3429690616e-02 

299 ) * v + 1.7004555372e-01 

300 core = c * (0.7853982 + (0.5 - 0.5 * v) * s) 

301 res = tl.where(a > 1.0, 1.5707964 - core, core) 

302 return ( 

303 res.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) | (x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) & -2147483648) 

304 ).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True) 

305 

306 

307@triton.jit 

308def _lgamma_pos_func(y): 

309 """``lgamma(y)`` for ``y > 0``: Stirling plus an 8-step recurrence. 

310 

311 The recurrence is what keeps the asymptotic series' argument large; the 

312 correction is ``log(y*(y+1)*...*(y+7))``. That product is 8 factors, so it 

313 stays inside fp32 up to ``y ~ 6e4``; above that the recurrence is skipped 

314 (its correction would be 0 anyway) and Stirling is evaluated at ``y``. 

315 """ 

316 prod = y * (y + 1.0) 

317 prod = prod * (y + 2.0) * (y + 3.0) 

318 prod = prod * (y + 4.0) * (y + 5.0) 

319 prod = prod * (y + 6.0) * (y + 7.0) 

320 shift = y < 60000.0 

321 z = tl.where(shift, y + 8.0, y) 

322 inv = tl_extra_shim.fast_dividef(1.0, z) 

323 inv2 = inv * inv 

324 st = (z - 0.5) * tl_extra_shim.fast_logf(z) - z + 0.9189385332046727 

325 st = st + inv * ( 

326 0.08333333333333333 

327 - inv2 * (0.002777777777777778 - inv2 * 0.0007936507936507937) 

328 ) 

329 corr = tl.where(shift, tl_extra_shim.fast_logf(prod), 0.0) 

330 return st - corr 

331 

332 

333@triton.jit 

334def _approx_lgamma_func(x): 

335 """``lgamma(x)``: log-magnitude, matching ATen's gammaln semantics. 

336 

337 The reflection uses ``sin`` (accurate), see the section comment; the poles 

338 (0 and the negative integers) and ``+-inf`` map to ``+inf`` and NaN 

339 propagates, both as ATen does. 

340 """ 

341 x = x.to(tl.float32) 

342 reflect = x < 0.5 

343 y = tl.where(reflect, 1.0 - x, x) 

344 pos = _lgamma_pos_func(y) 

345 # sin(pi*x), argument reduced to [-pi/2, pi/2]. ``sin`` (like 

346 # ``fast_logf`` below) flushes an fp32 subnormal argument to zero, and a 

347 # bf16 subnormal (down to ~9e-41) times pi is one -- exactly the tiny-|x| 

348 # reflection. There sin(z) == z to well below fp32 epsilon (relative 

349 # correction z^2/6 <= 2e-14 for |z| < 1e-7), so the linear branch is exact 

350 # and keeps the logarithm finite. 

351 reduced = x - tl.floor(x + 0.5) 

352 z = 3.1415927 * reduced 

353 sin_pi = tl.where(tl.abs(reduced) < 1.0e-7, z, tl_extra_shim.sin(z)) 

354 # ``fast_logf`` is ``lg2.approx``, which also flushes a subnormal input; 

355 # scaling by 2^64 (exact power-of-two multiply, |sin| <= 1 so no overflow) 

356 # keeps the log finite. Without this 80 bf16 inputs came out +inf against 

357 # ATen's ~90. 

358 log_sin = ( 

359 tl_extra_shim.fast_logf(tl.abs(sin_pi) * 18446744073709551616.0) 

360 - 44.3614195558365 

361 ) 

362 refl = 1.1447298858494002 - log_sin - pos 

363 res = tl.where(reflect, refl, pos) 

364 pole = (x <= 0.0) & (x == tl.floor(x)) 

365 return tl.where(pole | (tl.abs(x) == float("inf")), float("inf"), res) 

366

368# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

369# math not available as a reusable pointwise_dynamic scalar function 

370# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

371# 

372# ``round`` and ``sign`` are implemented in FlagGems as hand-written kernels 

373# rather than ``pointwise_dynamic``, so there is no scalar function to borrow. 

374# ``rsqrt`` does have one, but its ``1.0 / tl.sqrt(x)`` form keeps a 

375# full-precision divide where ``tl.rsqrt`` is available. 

376# 

377# ``tan`` keeps the borrowed scalar function. A ``sin/cos`` quotient was tried 

378# and rejected: on this device it takes 1.25x to 1.94x the kernel time of the 

379# generic libdevice body at every size measured (the extern already shares its 

380# range reduction across the two calls it makes, so the quotient pays for it 

381# twice), and the size gate that would have masked the small-tensor case only 

382# moved the regression above the gate. 

383 

384 

385@triton.jit 

386def _round_func(x): 

387 # Integral inputs are already rounded; float ones go through libdevice's 

388 # ``rint``, which is round-half-to-even and measured bitwise identical to 

389 # ``torch.round`` on 24k exact ties per dtype (both signs, including 

390 # ``+-0.5``) and on random data in fp32/fp16/bf16. The previous emulation 

391 # (floor + parity test + select) needed about eight instructions and got 

392 # the sign of a zero result wrong; ``rint`` is one. ``rint`` has no 16-bit 

393 # overload, so those widen first; ``float64`` is called directly because 

394 # widening it to float32 would round large values that the emulation used 

395 # to round exactly. 

396 if x.dtype == tl.float64: 

397 return tl_extra_shim.rint(x) 

398 elif x.dtype.is_floating(): 

399 return tl_extra_shim.rint(x.to(tl.float32)).to(x.dtype) 

400 else: 

401 return x 

402 

403 

404@triton.jit 

405def _rsqrt_func(x): 

406 # ``tl.rsqrt`` measured bitwise identical to ``torch.rsqrt`` on fp32, fp16 

407 # and bf16 over the suite's sample range and on grids near 1e-6 and 1.0; 

408 # the reused scalar function spells it as ``1.0 / tl.sqrt(x)``, which 

409 # leaves a full-precision divide in the body. Triton flushes fp32 

410 # denormals, so inputs below 2**-126 give inf here -- the base expression 

411 # does the same, so this is not a regression. 

412 return tl.rsqrt(x.to(tl.float32)) 

413 

414 

415@triton.jit 

416def _sign_func(x): 

417 # Mirrors ops/sign.py: NaN yields 0 because neither comparison holds. 

418 if x.dtype == tl.int1: 

419 return x 

420 elif x.dtype == tl.bfloat16: 

421 # Some backends cannot lower a direct i1-to-bf16 conversion. 

422 return tl.where(x > 0, 1.0, tl.where(x < 0, -1.0, 0.0)).to(x.dtype) 

423 else: 

424 return (x > 0).to(x.dtype) - (x < 0).to(x.dtype) 

425 

426 

427@triton.jit 

428def _abs_func(x): 

429 return tl.abs(x) 

430 

431 

432@triton.jit 

433def _abs_complex_func(re, im): 

434 # Modulus of a complex value. The executor passes the real and imaginary 

435 # components separately because Triton has no complex dtype. 

436 return _hypot_fn(re, im)

439# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

440# 16-bit fast-math path 

441# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

442# 

443# ``tl.log``/``tl.log2``/``tl.cos``/... lower to the IEEE-accurate libdevice 

444# entry points, which spend roughly 20-25 fp32 instructions per element on 

445# range reduction and a polynomial. libdevice also exports the SFU ("fast") 

446# variants: one MUFU instruction plus a cheap fixed-point range reduction. At 

447# 512^2 x 16 the fp16 unary call sits well above the 12.4 us copy floor 

448# (``log_`` 17.0 us), so the difference is worth 3.5-4.0 us of kernel time. 

449# 

450# Taking that trade is only defensible when the *output* is 16-bit. fp16 has 

451# ~5e-4 relative resolution and the suite tolerance is rtol=1e-3/atol=1e-4 

452# (bf16 rtol=1.6e-2), while the fast paths measure max abs error 7.6e-6 on 

453# ``log`` and 6.1e-5 on ``cos`` -- two orders of magnitude inside tolerance. 

454# They are not bit-exact against ATen at 16 bits, so the accurate function 

455# remains the default: the fast one is selected by dtype, never by operator. 

456# 

457# ``fast_log1pf`` does not exist. The accurate ``log1p`` body is already 

458# ``log(1 + x)``, so the fast version keeps that exact shape and changes only 

459# the log entry point -- the cancellation behaviour is inherited, not new. 

460# Likewise there is no fast ``erf``/``erfc``; those rows keep the accurate 

461# function. ``exp``/``expm1``/``sigmoid`` gain nothing because ``exp`` is 

462# already one cheap instruction. ``tanh`` has no usable fast extern (see its 

463# body) and is built from ``fast_expf`` instead. ``cosh`` was built the same 

464# way and then dropped: libdevice ``coshf`` is already within ~1 us of the copy 

465# floor, and ABBA at 512^2 in-place measured +0.04 us for the fast body, level 

466# with the untouched ``sinh`` control (+0.38), so it is noise rather than a win. 

467# 

468# The executor hands these functions a value already cast to the output 

469# dtype, so every body widens to fp32 first: the libdevice fast entry points 

470# have no 16-bit overload. 

471# 

472# ``fn16`` is consumed by the in-place entry point only. An out-of-place call 

473# already spends more host time than ``do_bench``'s L2-flush window, so extra 

474# Python in the dispatch leaks into the measured latency while the kernel time 

475# the fast body saves stays hidden under it; measured, enabling it there turned 

476# every out-of-place row into a 1.3-3.7 us regression at 512^2. The accurate 

477# body is free on that path, so out-of-place deliberately keeps ``op.fn``. Do 

478# not "restore the symmetry" -- see ``apply_unary``. 

479 

480 

481@triton.jit 

482def _fast_log_func(x): 

483 return tl_extra_shim.fast_logf(x.to(tl.float32)) 

484 

485 

486@triton.jit 

487def _fast_log2_func(x): 

488 return tl_extra_shim.fast_log2f(x.to(tl.float32)) 

489 

490 

491@triton.jit 

492def _fast_log10_func(x): 

493 # The accurate body is ``tl.log(x) * log10(e)``; the direct entry point 

494 # also saves the extra multiply. 

495 return tl_extra_shim.fast_log10f(x.to(tl.float32)) 

496 

497 

498@triton.jit 

499def _fast_log1p_func(x): 

500 return tl_extra_shim.fast_logf(1.0 + x.to(tl.float32)) 

501 

502 

503@triton.jit 

504def _fast_cos_func(x): 

505 return tl_extra_shim.fast_cosf(x.to(tl.float32)) 

506 

507 

508@triton.jit 

509def _fast_sin_func(x): 

510 return tl_extra_shim.fast_sinf(x.to(tl.float32)) 

511 

512 

513@triton.jit 

514def _fast_tan_func(x): 

515 return tl_extra_shim.fast_tanf(x.to(tl.float32)) 

516 

517 

518@triton.jit 

519def _fast_tanh_func(x): 

520 # ``tanh`` spends the same accurate-``exp`` budget as the log family; at 

521 # 512^2 fp16 the reused kernel measured 2.7 us of ALU over the copy floor. 

522 # The obvious ``fast_tanhf`` is not usable here: the Python module exports 

523 # the name, but the extern it lowers to (``__nv_fast_tanhf``) is not in this 

524 # CUDA toolkit's device library, so ptxas fails the link with "Unresolved 

525 # extern function". This is the standard SFU identity, one ``fast_expf`` 

526 # plus a reciprocal: ``2 / (1 + e^-2x) - 1``. Written in this direction 

527 # because the algebraically equivalent ``(e^2x - 1) / (e^2x + 1)`` turns 

528 # into ``inf / inf`` = NaN for large inputs, while this form saturates to 

529 # +-1 exactly as ``tanh`` does. At the 512^2 x 16 randn distribution it 

530 # disagrees with the accurate path on 0.02% of lanes (99.98% bit-identical 

531 # at fp16, max abs 1.2e-4, inside the suite's rtol=1e-3/atol=1e-4). 

532 return 1.0 - 2.0 / (tl_extra_shim.fast_expf(2.0 * x.to(tl.float32)) + 1.0) 

533 

534 

535# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

536# dtype sets, as measured 

537# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

538 

539_FLOAT = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64) 

540_INT = (torch.int8, torch.int16, torch.int32, torch.int64, torch.uint8) 

541_COMPLEX = (torch.complex32, torch.complex64, torch.complex128) 

542 

543# Everything except complex: erf / erfc / lgamma / sign. 

544NO_COMPLEX = frozenset(_FLOAT + _INT + (torch.bool,)) 

545# Integral dtypes are fine, bool is not: ceil / floor / round / trunc. 

546NO_BOOL_NO_COMPLEX = frozenset(_FLOAT + _INT) 

547# Floating point only: frac. 

548FLOAT_ONLY = frozenset(_FLOAT) 

549# Everything except bool: neg. 

550NO_BOOL = frozenset(_FLOAT + _INT + (torch.complex64, torch.complex128)) 

551# Transcendentals: complex64/128 work, complex32 does not. Measured -- only 

552# ``abs`` accepts complex32 in this build, ComplexHalf being experimental. 

553NO_COMPLEX32 = frozenset( 

554 _FLOAT + _INT + (torch.bool, torch.complex64, torch.complex128) 

555) 

556 

557 

558class UnaryOp: 

559 """One row of the unary foreach table.""" 

560 

561 __slots__ = ("name", "fn", "out_dtype_fn", "allowed", "complex_fn", "fn16") 

562 

563 def __init__( 

564 self, 

565 name: str, 

566 fn: Callable, 

567 out_dtype_fn: Callable = int_to_float, 

568 allowed: Optional[frozenset] = None, 

569 complex_fn: Optional[Callable] = None, 

570 fn16: Optional[Callable] = None, 

571 ) -> None: 

572 self.name = name 

573 self.fn = fn 

574 self.out_dtype_fn = out_dtype_fn 

575 self.allowed = allowed 

576 self.complex_fn = complex_fn 

577 # Alternate, lower-accuracy function used only when every input is 

578 # 16-bit; ``None`` means the row has no fast variant. 

579 self.fn16 = fn16 

580 

581 

582UNARY_OPS: Dict[str, UnaryOp] = { 

583 op.name: op 

584 for op in ( 

585 UnaryOp("abs", _abs_func, real_dtype_of, None, _abs_complex_func), 

586 UnaryOp("acos", _scalar_fn(acos_kernel), int_to_float, NO_COMPLEX32, c_acos), 

587 UnaryOp("asin", _scalar_fn(asin_kernel), int_to_float, NO_COMPLEX32, c_asin), 

588 UnaryOp( 

589 "atan", 

590 _atan_func, 

591 int_to_float, 

592 NO_COMPLEX32, 

593 c_atan, 

594 fn16=_atan16_func, 

595 ), 

596 UnaryOp("ceil", _scalar_fn(ceil_func), same_dtype, NO_BOOL_NO_COMPLEX), 

597 UnaryOp( 

598 "cos", 

599 _scalar_fn(cos_func), 

600 int_to_float, 

601 NO_COMPLEX32, 

602 c_cos, 

603 fn16=_fast_cos_func, 

604 ), 

605 UnaryOp("cosh", _scalar_fn(cosh_func), int_to_float, NO_COMPLEX32, c_cosh), 

606 UnaryOp( 

607 "erf", 

608 _scalar_fn(erf_func), 

609 int_to_float, 

610 NO_COMPLEX, 

611 fn16=_approx_erf_func, 

612 ), 

613 UnaryOp( 

614 "erfc", 

615 _scalar_fn(_erfc_kernel), 

616 int_to_float, 

617 NO_COMPLEX, 

618 fn16=_approx_erfc_func, 

619 ), 

620 UnaryOp("exp", _scalar_fn(exp_func), int_to_float, NO_COMPLEX32, c_exp), 

621 UnaryOp("expm1", _scalar_fn(expm1_func), int_to_float, NO_COMPLEX32, c_expm1), 

622 UnaryOp("floor", _scalar_fn(floor_func), same_dtype, NO_BOOL_NO_COMPLEX), 

623 UnaryOp("frac", _scalar_fn(frac_func), same_dtype, FLOAT_ONLY), 

624 UnaryOp( 

625 "lgamma", 

626 _scalar_fn(lgamma_func), 

627 int_to_float, 

628 NO_COMPLEX, 

629 fn16=_approx_lgamma_func, 

630 ), 

631 UnaryOp( 

632 "log", 

633 _scalar_fn(log_func), 

634 int_to_float, 

635 NO_COMPLEX32, 

636 c_log, 

637 fn16=_fast_log_func, 

638 ), 

639 UnaryOp( 

640 "log10", 

641 _scalar_fn(log10_func), 

642 int_to_float, 

643 NO_COMPLEX32, 

644 c_log10, 

645 fn16=_fast_log10_func, 

646 ), 

647 UnaryOp( 

648 "log1p", 

649 _scalar_fn(log1p_func), 

650 int_to_float, 

651 NO_COMPLEX32, 

652 c_log1p, 

653 fn16=_fast_log1p_func, 

654 ), 

655 UnaryOp( 

656 "log2", 

657 _scalar_fn(log2_func), 

658 int_to_float, 

659 NO_COMPLEX32, 

660 c_log2, 

661 fn16=_fast_log2_func, 

662 ), 

663 UnaryOp("neg", _scalar_fn(neg_func), same_dtype, NO_BOOL, c_neg), 

664 UnaryOp( 

665 "reciprocal",

667 int_to_float,

676 int_to_float,

711 

712def apply_unary(name: str, self, inplace: bool): 

713 """Dispatch one table row through the shared executor.""" 

714 op = UNARY_OPS[name] 

715 logger.debug("GEMS _FOREACH_%s%s", name.upper(), "_" if inplace else "") 

716 if inplace: 

717 # The alternate function is only valid when the result is 16-bit, and the 

718 # executor casts each input to its own output dtype, so "16-bit result" 

719 # means "every input is fp16/bf16". The test runs inside this loop 

720 # rather than as a separate pass because the loop already touches every 

721 # tensor for the complex check; a second walk would cost host time that 

722 # the in-place call cannot afford to spend. 

723 # 

724 # Per-tensor, not ``self[0].dtype``: a list that mixes fp16 with fp32 

725 # must take the accurate path, and the executor's bucketing path shares 

726 # one ``fn`` across dtype groups. 

727 # 

728 # Only the in-place entry point uses this. An out-of-place call already 

729 # spends past the do_bench L2-flush window on host work, so added Python 

730 # leaks 1:1 into its measured latency while the kernel time saved by the 

731 # fast body stays hidden underneath it -- gated on that path the change 

732 # measured as a 1.3-3.7 us regression. The accurate body costs it 

733 # nothing, so out-of-place keeps ``op.fn`` unconditionally. 

734 # 

735 # Every ``fn16`` body below is built on a vendor libdevice ``fast_*`` 

736 # entry point, so the path is also gated on the backend being able to 

737 # lower them at all -- see ``_FAST_MATH_OK``. 

738 fast = op.fn16 is not None and _FAST_MATH_OK 

739 for t in self: 

740 if t.dtype.is_complex and op.out_dtype_fn is real_dtype_of: 

741 raise RuntimeError( 

742 f"In-place {name} is not supported for complex tensors." 

743 ) 

744 if fast and t.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16): 

745 fast = False 

746 fn = op.fn16 if fast else op.fn 

747 foreach_unary( 

748 self, 

749 fn, 

750 complex_fn=op.complex_fn, 

751 # The dtype policy has to be passed here too: it is what makes the 

752 # executor reject an integral in-place call on a promoting operator, 

753 # matching ATen's "result type Float can't be cast to the desired 

754 # output type Long". Omitting it silently accepted int64 sin_. 

755 out_dtype_fn=op.out_dtype_fn, 

756 inplace=True, 

757 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

758 ) 

759 # The in-place schemas return ``()``; returning the list makes the 

760 # dispatcher reject the kernel. 

761 return None 

762 return foreach_unary( 

763 self, 

764 op.fn, 

765 complex_fn=op.complex_fn, 

766 out_dtype_fn=op.out_dtype_fn, 

767 allowed_dtypes=op.allowed, 

768 ) 

769 

770
